card.title: How To Fix an iPhone 13 That Randomly Restarts

source.title: How To Fix an iPhone 13 That Randomly Restarts

claims.statement: On iPhone 13 series, read the SMC PANIC assertion's Sensor Array hex value in the panic-full log.
0x1000 = proximity flex; 0x800 = charging port flex; 0x1800 = both.
0x4000 = battery data line issue (fluctuating percentage or non-genuine message); check connector pins, compare diode readings, try a known-good battery or replace the connector.
0x400 (13 mini only) = bottom-board gyroscope communication; rebuilding pads 207, 208, 502, 503, 504, 527 and 528 fixes it. 0xc00 (13 mini) = that plus the charging port flex.
Power button and charging port flexes must be connected or the phone always restarts (Wi-Fi antenna flex excepted).

procedure: Find the Sensor Array value in the SMC panic.
0x1000 prox flex / 0x800 charge flex / 0x1800 both: test known-good OEM flexes, diode-check FPCs.
0x4000: inspect and diode-check battery connector, try known-good battery.
0x400 / 0xc00 (mini): rebuild the listed bottom-board pads, plus fix charge flex for 0xc00.
card.caveats: Community-written Repair Wiki page, paraphrased; check the linked page (and its images) before acting on a reading.
card.component: Proximity flex / charge port flex / battery
